adversarial_probes.note: 8 edge-case probes run as temporary test (_adversarial_probe.test.ts, deleted post-run). All 10 assertions passed.

probes.description: alg=RS256 in JWT header but EC key published at that kid in JWKS (key-type confusion)
probes.actual: 401 — verifyRsaSignature uses crypto.createPublicKey({format:'jwk'}) which rejects EC JWK as RSA; returns false → 401

probes.description: kid points to absent key in non-empty JWKS — forceRefresh triggered once, then 401 (no infinite loop)
probes.actual: 401; fetch count ≤ 4 (discovery + certs × 2 for initial + force-refresh); terminates correctly

probes.description: JWKS response with empty keys[] — no key for kid=undefined fallback
probes.actual: 401 unknown signing key — keys[0] is undefined, matchingKey stays undefined
Processed without crash; large payload passes through JSON.parse safely
verifyJwt returns claims — aud.includes(audience) works for arrays

probes.description: exp = now - 61 (1 second beyond 60s clock-skew tolerance)
probes.actual: 401 token expired — condition: exp + 60 < nowSecs → (now-61)+60 = now-1 < now → true
verifyJwt returns claims — (now-59)+60 = now+1 > now → within tolerance
401 UNAUTHENTICATED — lowercase 'bearer' does not match 'Bearer ' prefix check

probes.expected: Behavior: .slice(7).trim() extracts token correctly → accepted if token is valid
probes.actual: 201 — double space handled: slice(7) = ' <token>', trim() = '<token>'; valid token accepted
probes.note: This is a permissive behavior: double-space is silently normalised. Not a security issue (token still fully validated), documented here for transparency.
